boundaryDeclaration.h1Historical: No trusted factory => core decision keeps exactly one pre-step, one request, one stream, zero tools and the original accounting rule; dispatch/tool phases are never entered.
boundaryDeclaration.h2cNew: A trusted host factory for the admitted Goal binding may mount exactly three read-only event tools (types, subscriptions, report-observation). The round then allows at most ONE event-tool call and at most TWO main model requests/streams: request 1 -> one assistant tool-call -> one matching native tool/result pair -> request 2 -> one final text JSON candidate.
boundaryDeclaration.alternation: The second main request is admitted only after exactly one completed tool call/result whose call id, name, raw arguments and native result message hash match the recorded events. A duplicate tool-call block, a second tool/call, a second tool round, missing result, forged authority arguments or a revoked/paused authority check fail the round explicitly.
boundaryDeclaration.budget: The second request maxTokens is the remaining output budget: maxTokens minus the first assistant message outputTokens. If the first assistant usage/outputTokens is missing, the second request is refused as unknown rather than guessing or zero-padding. The native per-request output ceiling and the overall run budget stay enforced.
boundaryDeclaration.finalCandidate: The plan/candidate is still one final assistant text JSON response within the same turn; tool results never become Task/Goal facts or authorization. The core domain commit/plan CAS/unknown/pause/revoke paths are untouched and still validate the final text.
boundaryDeclaration.accounting: Main model requests/streams and tool calls are separately observable in CoreDecisionAccounting (mainModelRequests/mainModelStreams/toolCalls/toolResults/eventToolCalls/toolNames). modelCalls is the observed main-request count only when coverage is complete, otherwise null. Tokens are summed only when every main assistant usage is complete; unknown coverage stays complete:false with tokens/calls absent. Durable accounting evidenceRef encodes main/streams/tools/results counts and never substitutes zero for unknown.
boundaryDeclaration.replyerWorkerUnchanged: replyer remains zero-tool; worker restricted tool budget and zero-model worker probe are unchanged by H2c.

positives: types query -> final plan_candidate: exactly three mounted schemas, 2 requests/2 streams, maxTokens [512,505], one provider execution with host context, accounting reported tokens 38 and tool counts 1/1, plan candidate text unchanged and no Task/Goal change.
no-tool path: mounted but unused surface keeps 1 request/1 stream, tokens 18, toolCalls 0, complete accounting.
report observation: a real provider publishes one scoped agent.observation.reported with host-injected actor; no task.succeeded and no authoritative fact; tool result is data only.
zero-tool fallback without factory: historical single-request decision remains fully usable and assembly is tool-free.
core service probe delegates to the trusted adapter and refuses while paused (same admission semantics as other probes).
negatives: duplicate tool-call blocks in one assistant message -> round rejected, no provider execution, accounting unknown with modelCalls null.
second tool/call (second round) -> rejected, exactly the first provider execution happened, no second provider call.
missing first-response usage -> second request refused as unknown; accounting complete:false, tokens/calls absent, no zero padding.
paused/revoked authority at the tool phase -> tool provider not executed, no accepted event, accounting unknown.
authority-looking tool arguments (scope/permit/actor/ownerId/taskId) -> rejected before provider execution.
reserved/authorative report types (task.succeeded, component-only types) -> rejected by the mounted surface; no accepted event.
overbroad provider schema (authority field) / non-exact tool set -> rejected before dispatch, followup/stream counts 0.
provider report grant including reserved types or subscription target refs -> provider construction fails closed.
disposable probe cleanup failure is explicit; cancelled/late probe handle is cancelled and disposed.

runtimeIntegration.file: plugins/shiyu/src/runtime.ts (Lead lands; not edited by this slice)
runtimeIntegration.purpose: Supply the trusted per-Goal core event tool factory to LocalCoreService and expose the owner-only zero-model mount diagnostic.
runtimeIntegration.precondition: Create the factory after `this.events = new EventService(this.store);` and pass it into the LocalCoreOptions used to construct LocalCoreService (currently around runtime.ts:262). The factory must stay in trusted composition; never accept it from command JSON. The probe command uses the existing session.probe admission semantics (rejected while globally paused, one shared operation slot, abortable, no retry) and performs no model/embedding/Task/Goal/Lab action.
runtimeIntegration.failureDegradation: No factory => core decisions stay on the historical zero-tool path. A factory/provider validation failure rejects only that decision round before dispatch. The probe command reports CORE_EVENT_TOOL_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE when the driver lacks the probe and stores no receipt; a failing probe sets lastFailure and leaves diagnostics unchanged.

zeroModelHostProbeChecklist.limitation: A zero-model probe proves mount/restrictions/release only. It cannot prove a real model called the tools, that provider budgets/cache were honoured, that the final plan was semantically valid, or that tool results stayed non-authoritative in a real model run. Those remain G4/bounded-real-model gaps.
